approved.oldValue: Ram Katha is a multi-day public recitation of the Ramcharitmanas — Tulsidas's 16th-century retelling of the Ramayana in Awadhi — performed by a trained kathavachak (narrator). Once a year, the [[ram-mandir-thakurbari|Ram Mandir Thakurbari]] in Bandwar hosts one such Katha, and the entire village gathers to listen. Ram Katha is not unique to Bandwar — it is a common practice across North India, especially in the Hindi belt — but the Katha at Thakurbari has particular significance for Bandwar, because the temple where it is held is the village's principal Ram temple.

approved.oldValue: Once a year, the [[ram-mandir-thakurbari|Ram Mandir Thakurbari]] hosts a Ram Katha — a multi-day public recitation of the Ramcharitmanas by a trained narrator. The 2021 edition was attended by the entire village, and was held under a pink-and-white striped pandal in the temple courtyard. The Katha is one of the most important religious events in the village calendar, reflecting the deep Vaishnavite tradition of the Mithila region.
